bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Union of International Associations (UIA), the Union des associations internationales (UAI) in French, is a nonprofit research institute and documentation center on the work of global civil philanthropy and society. The UIA promotes international collaboration, peace, security and sustainability through documentation and networking activities. It is based in Brussels, Belgium. The UIA was founded in 1907 by Nobel Peace Prize winner Henri La Fontaine and father of information science Paul Otlet. The UIA has roots in other institutions established by La Fontaine and Otlet in 1895, the International Institute of Bibliography and the Répertoire Bibliographique Universel.

Each year, the UIA publishes the Yearbook of International Organizations which provides information on more than 45,000 active organizations from 300 countries and territories, including intergovernmental and international non-governmental organizations. The UIA has been documenting international civil society since 1908 when it partnered with the Institut International de Bibliographie and the Institut International de la Paix to publish the 1908 and 1909 editions of the Annuaire de la Vie Internationale, a precursor to the Yearbook of International Organizations.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Union of International Associations (UIA) collection includes the UIA's premier annual publication, the Yearbook of International Organizations, the files of Henri La Fontaine, one of UIA's founders, the files of Georges Patrick Speeckaert and Robert Fenaux, secretary-generals of UIA, the UIA journal Transnational Associations and International Associations from 1969-2003, photographs, the International Congress Calendars publication, books and reference materials published by UIA, circulaires and correspondence with international organizations, and materials related to UIA's organizational history. The collection spans from 1892-2026. The newest edition of the Yearbook of International Associations will be added to the collection as received each year.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: This material was transferred to RAC in 2025 and 2026 by the Union of International Associations (UIA) and ingested by RAC as Accessions 2025:065, 2025:071, and 2026:001. The collection has been processed as FA1935.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Original folder titles in their original languages have been maintained when possible. Description created by archivists is in English.

did.unittitle: Yearbook of International Organizations

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series contains copies of the Yearbook of International Organizations, the Union of International Association's resource for describing international nonprofit organizations. The series holds the Yearbook from its first edition published in 1948 to its most recent release. The series also contains the Yearbook's predecessor publication, the Office Central des Institutions Internationales, Annuaire de la Vie Internationale beginning in 1908.

Early editions of the Yearbook have full English and French language translations. Starting around the 1980s, editions encompass multiple volumes with each volume having its own function like providing descriptions for different organizations or a subject guide. Scope notes describe the focus of each volume. There appear to be some minor gaps in regards to some editions' volume completion.

did.unittitle: Henri La Fontaine
did.langmaterial: Materials primarily in French. Some materials in English, German, Japanese, and Dutch.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Henri La Fontaine was born on April 22, 1854. He studied law at the Free University of Brussels, and in 1893, he became a professor of international law at the Free University of Brussels. In 1895, he was elected to the Belgian Senate as a member of the Socialist Party. La Fontaine was president of the International Peace Bureau from 1907 until his death in 1943. In 1913, he received the Nobel Peace Prize "for his unparalleled contribution to the organization of peaceful internationalism." He was a member of the Belgian delegation to the Paris Peace Conference in 1919 and to the League of Nations Assembly in 1920. He founded the Centre Intellectuel Mondial, and in 1907, he founded the Union of International Associations with Paul Otlet, a Belgian author, lawyer and peace activist who is considered one of the early leaders in the field of information science. La Fontaine and Otlet also founded the Institut International de Bibliographie. La Fontaine died on May 1943 in Brussels.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The series contains correspondence, reports, newspaper clippings, pamphlets, and memorabilia related to international relations and efforts toward world peace during the 1910s-1940s. Many materials correspond to Henri La Fontaine's attendance at international meetings, particularly meetings associated with the League of Nations. The series also highlights the Union of International Association's efforts to secure funding from the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. The series contains correspondence and notes regarding the creation of the Annuaire de la Vie Internationale. The series also contains some of La Fontaine's publications.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Georges Patrick "G.P." Speeckaert studied law in Louvain, Belgium. During World War II, Speeckaert was a prisoner of war in Germany, active in the Resistance movement, and following the war, he served as head of the Department of Social Services of the Red Cross which worked to rebuild Belgium in the war's aftermath.

Speeckaert served as the head of the secretariat of UIA in 1948 upon the resumption of regular UIA activities following the deaths of founders Paul Otlet and Henri La Fontaine. While in this role, he was also administrative secretary of the International Colonial Institute. In 1952, he became secretary-general of UIA and held that position until 1970.

At UIA, Speeckaert worked to secure international and domestic funding for the organization. He also inventoried the archives, revived the Annuaire des Organisations Internationales, later the Yearbook of International Organizations, published a Monthly Bulletin with a calendar of international meetings, and organized a survey of international organizations.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The series contains the files of Union of International Associations (UIA) Secretary General, Robert Fenaux. Fenaux's files chiefly concern UIA membership, funding, and meetings as well as the international NGO field. The series includes legacy material from Fenaux's Secretary General predecessor Georges Patrick Speeckaert which Fenaux carried over into his work.
Files show the UIA keeping track of its membership and its members' contributions. There are also files concerning grant applications and funding from governments.

Meetings documented in the files include internal UIA meetings of its Steering Committee and General Assembly as well as external meetings and conferences. These external meetings concerned NGOS and international philanthropy. Several files in the series were created to document the UIA's communications and work with NGOs and intergovernmental organizations like the United Nations.

Material formats found within the series include correspondence, transcripts of speeches Fenaux gave, reports, proposals, drafts, meeting materials, brochures, and publications. There are also a few photographs.

Circulaires and Correspondence

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains circulaires and correspondence files created by the Union of International Associations (UIA) primarily between the 1950s and the early 1970s.

The bulk of the circulaires in the series are contained in a numbered system that spans from 1956 to 1970. There are also a few circulaires housed with other published documents at the start of the series. Circulaires are documents about the UIA's operations.

The correspondence in the series is organized around specific topics like the Yearbook of International Organizations, the International Congress Calendar, bibliographies of proceedings of international meetings, and other publications. There is also some general correspondence.
Contained with the correspondence and circulaires are also reports, proposals, drafts, press clippings, and publications.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The series contains various materials pertaining to the organizational history of the Union of International Associations (UIA). There are descriptions of the organization, its work, and its members. These materials come in the form of UIA statutes, leaflets, publications, outlines, and press. There are also materials documenting the early work of the UIA and its research projects on international organizations.
